subject: Scheduler starvation affecting reserved GPU pool — remediation and timelines
messages:
From: Samuel Patel <samuel.patel@vertexretail.com>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.com>
Cc: Legal Ops <contracts@vertexretail.com>
Date: 2026-12-08T09:15:00-08:00
Subject: Re: High error rate and timeouts on reserved GPU pool this morning

Hi Sofia,

We started seeing a spike in failed requests to our dedicated pool around 08:50 PST — several of our inference calls returned 503s and median latency jumped from ~180ms to >1.2s. The errors are intermittent but enough to affect our checkout flow. I attached a short sample of the logs showing request IDs and timestamps.

Can your team confirm whether this is an issue on the Redwood side (scheduler/eviction) or something in our model container? We haven't made any changes on our side since last week. We also see a short blip in instance warmups followed by requests that queue for long periods.

This is high-impact for us — can you share an ETA for a mitigation?

Thanks,
Sam Patel
Senior Platform Engineer
Vertex Retail

[Attachment: vertex-logs-sample.txt (plain text, 12KB)]

From: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.com>
To: Samuel Patel <samuel.patel@vertexretail.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-12-08T09:42:00-08:00
Subject: Re: High error rate and timeouts on reserved GPU pool this morning

Hi Sam — thank you for the quick heads up and the log snippet. We’ve prioritized this incident and I’m looping in our on-call infra and the Dedicated Capacity team. Initial findings: there is evidence of scheduler starvation within your reserved node pool during the 08:45—09:05 window, which caused short-lived request queueing and increased latency. We do not see any changes from your model image that would explain this.

Immediate mitigations we’ve applied (done at 09:30 PST):
- Temporarily increased warm standby nodes for your pool to reduce scheduling contention.
- Enabled a short autoscale override to allow faster node provisioning until we stabilize.
- Applied a throttling cap for large-batch requests from a small subset of request IDs to limit burst-induced headroom exhaustion.

We are continuing to collect traces and will follow up with a timeline for root cause and permanent fix. I’ve attached the pool headroom snapshot and a short diagnostic summary so you have the same telemetry we’re looking at.

Next steps from us:
1) Ops will complete a detailed timeline and callback by EOD today (PST).
2) We’ll provide a proposed remediation and a proposal for a goodwill credit if there is an SLA impact.
3) We'll share the postmortem draft within 48 hours and schedule a 30‑minute review with your infra + platform team.

Apologies for the disruption. I’ll keep you posted as soon as we have the timeline.

—
Sofia Ivanova
Customer Reliability Lead, Dedicated Capacity
Redwood Inference

[Attachments: pool_headroom_snapshot_20261208.json, initial-diagnostics-summary.txt]

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Samuel Patel <samuel.patel@vertexretail.com>
Cc: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-12-08T13:05:00-08:00
Subject: RE: High error rate and timeouts on reserved GPU pool this morning

Hi Sam — quick ops update and the mitigations timeline.

Root-cause (interim):
- Scheduler starvation inside the reserved pool's placement queue. A small set of high-concurrency requests caused continuous rebalancing of KV caches and prevented efficient packing of incoming tasks for ~20 minutes.

What we did by 09:30 PST:
- Bypassed the affected scheduler shard and shifted new small requests to warm nodes.
- Temporarily disabled a recently-deployed aggressive compaction heuristic that, under certain concurrency patterns, increased placement churn.

Impact window: ~08:45 — 09:05 PST; 12–18% of your requests in that window saw latency >750ms or 5xx errors.

Compensatory offer:
We want to make this right. If post-investigation confirms an SLA breach we will:
- Issue a one-time account credit equal to 5% of December's Reserved Capacity monthly invoice, or
- Alternatively, apply a 30% service-credit for the impacted hours (your preference).

Deliverables and timeline:
- Full incident timeline and root-cause analysis by EOD tomorrow (2026-12-09).
- Postmortem draft shared by 2026-12-10 with an engineering remediation plan and a regression test added to our canary harness.
- 30‑minute review call to walk through the postmortem (we propose 2026-12-11 10:00 PST).

Please reply with your preference on the credit option and confirm availability for the review call.

Best,
Ben Carter
Sr. Incident Response Engineer
Redwood Inference

[Attachment: credit-offer-VertexRetail-20261210.pdf]

From: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.com>
To: Samuel Patel <samuel.patel@vertexretail.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-12-10T16:42:00-08:00
Subject: Follow-up: postmortem and remediation plan (SUP-9873)

Hi Sam — thank you again for your patience. Attached is the postmortem draft (postmortem-draft-vertex-20261210.pdf) and a brief remediation checklist we’ll implement over the next two weeks. High-level summary:

- Root cause: scheduler shard compaction heuristic triggered excessive rebalancing under a particular concurrency pattern from your workload. That rebalancing increased placement churn and prevented efficient packing, causing momentary headroom exhaustion.
- Permanent mitigations: revert compaction heuristic, add a placement-stability guard, and extend warm-standby thresholds for reserved pools that match your concurrency profile.
- Regression coverage: added a synthetic concurrency test to the canary harness and a short-running e2e scenario that simulates your peak request mix.

We have created Jira SUP-9873 with the commit plan and ETA: 2026-12-22 for the rollback+stability guard; monitoring and canary verification complete by 2026-12-23.

We’d like to schedule the 30-minute review for 2026-12-11 10:00 PST as Ben suggested — please confirm or propose an alternate slot. Also please let us know which compensatory credit option you prefer; we’ve attached the formal credit letter.

Postmortem link: https://drive.redwood.com/postmortems/vertex-20261210

Apologies again for the disruption. We’ll keep you updated as we close the Jira items and verify the regression protections.

—
Sofia Ivanova
Customer Reliability Lead, Dedicated Capacity
Redwood Inference

[Attachment: postmortem-draft-vertex-20261210.pdf]
